newsitem.title: NORWAY: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL ON COURSE TO JOIN ELITE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL ON COURSE TO JOIN ELITE.

text.p: Liverpool continue their campaign to join the elite band of teams to win all three European soccer competitions when they travel to Norwegian outsiders Brann Bergen in the quarter-finals of the Cup Winners' Cup on Thursday.

The four-times European champions and double UEFA Cup winners hope to join Juventus, Barcelona, Ajax and Bayern Munich in an exclusive club and look to have the ideal draw to progress. The part-timers of Brann have not played a competitive match since October -- although that completed an impressive two-leg victory over Dutch league leaders PSV Eindhoven.
They have spent the last two months training in warmer areas of Europe, most recently in Spain where they played against Spanish first and second division sides.
Coach Kjell Tennfjord will look to strikers Tore Andre Flo and Mons Ivar Mjelde to continue their prolific partnership.
Flo scored 19 goals last season while Mjelde has already notched up six in this European campaign.
Mjelde has had a bad dose of influenza but should recover in time for the match.

However, two players who definitely will not be taking part are Iceland international goalkeeper Birkir Kristinsson and midfielder Jan Ove Pederson, who were not re-registered in time after playing away on loan.
Liverpool have been in good form recently although their 1-0 defeat at Aston Villa on Sunday was a somewhat lacklustre display.

Manager Roy Evans is delaying naming his team until as late as possible but will have to shuffle his defence. Norwegian defender Bjorne Tore Kvarme is ineligible while Mark Wright injured a leg in the Villa game. Fit-again Irish international Phil Babb and Neil Ruddock look set to step in alongside Dominic Matteo.
Evans's main concern will be to keep a clean sheet but he will hope that Robbie Fowler rediscovers his goal touch should a chance arise.
The normally deadly striker has had some glaring misses in recent weeks and though his appetite and confidence appear undiminished, a goal would obviously be welcome.

Attitude, as much as ability, will be in demand on what is likely to be a bitterly cold night in the west of Norway. Fowler could never be accused of lacking in either department but his strike partner Stan Collymore is not renowned for digging deep when the going gets tough. Liverpool made their reputation in Europe by snuffing out sides away from home and destroying them at Anfield.
Evans, a member of the back row staff during those glory years, will hope for a similar show on Thursday.
